about: Fixed eval set for godot-bug-finder, written 18 Nov 2026. Every case comes from a real recorded run in examples/ except the two marked synthetic. Labels were written from the README's ground truth and by reading each report against signals.csv, before verify_report.py was run on the real reports. Failure cases are kept in on purpose: the point is to see them, not to score 100%.

detection.known_failure: A camera move at frames 46-47 trips the jump threshold: one false alarm.

detection.truth: Soft-lock fired at frame 55 (27 Sep live run 4).
A pop-up window covered the game at frame 34 (P(game) 0.53). No game bug: it is a harness event.
detection.known_failure: Frame 34 scored just over the 0.5 CLIP cut-off, so the overlay was flagged as a game sudden_jump.

detection.truth: Collision box offset 32 px. Not visible to pixel differences or a whole-frame CLIP check.
detection.out_of_scope: Listed so it is never forgotten. No run can score it until perception understands platforms.

reports.why: Its evidence note calls frames 34-157 'pixel-identical', but frame 34 is normal play from before the soft-lock (anomaly starts at 49), and the measured median change in the stretch is 0.91, not zero.
Right that it is a bug, wrong cause (a wall; the truth is a timer that pauses the game). It also calls frame 41 part of the frozen stretch, but the anomaly starts at 56.
Correctly 'not a real bug' but for the wrong reason: it blames normal movement and the camera. Frame 34 (P(game) 0.53, the pop-up) was never sent to it.

reports.note: No signals.csv in this example, so only the schema, kind, harness and frame checks can run.

synthetic_reports.about: Hand-written to make sure each check can fire. Not model output.

report.title: Game crashed
report.suspected_cause: Physics crash. Pixel change of 47.2 at frame 12.

synthetic_reports.about: A copy of run A report_000 with nothing changed except the title: the checker should leave it alone.
